Start working on Linear ticket eng-2227 by fetching its details and creating a dedicated git worktree.

## Steps

### 1. Validate input
- `eng-2227` should be a Linear ticket ID like `ENG-1271`. If missing or malformed, ask the user.

### 2. Fetch ticket details from Linear
- Use `mcp__linear-server__get_issue` with the issue ID `eng-2227`
- Extract: title, description, and `branchName` (Linear provides this)
- If the Linear tool is unavailable, ask the user for a branch name manually

### 3. Determine branch name
- Use the `branchName` field from Linear if available (it's already formatted correctly)
- Otherwise derive it: lowercase the ticket ID + hyphenated slug of the title
  - Example: `ENG-1271 Implement filter search` → `eng-1271-implement-filter-search`
  - Strip special characters, replace spaces with hyphens, truncate to ~60 chars

### 4. Create git worktree
Run these from the repo root (the main working directory, not an existing worktree):

```bash
# Fetch latest main so the worktree starts from up-to-date origin/main
git fetch origin main

# Check if branch already exists
git branch --list <branch-name>

# Check if worktree already exists
git worktree list | grep <branch-name>
```

- **If worktree already exists**: skip to step 5, just `cd` into `.claude/worktrees/<branch-name>`
- **If branch does NOT exist**: `git worktree add -b <branch-name> .claude/worktrees/<branch-name> origin/main`
- **If branch already exists but no worktree**: reset the branch to `origin/main` first, then add the worktree:
  ```bash
  git branch -f <branch-name> origin/main
  git worktree add .claude/worktrees/<branch-name> <branch-name>
  ```

### 5. Enter the worktree
**Do NOT use the `EnterWorktree` tool** — it always creates a brand-new worktree and will duplicate the one you just created.

Instead, use `cd` to switch into the worktree directory:
```bash
cd .claude/worktrees/<branch-name>
```

All subsequent commands should run from this path.

### 6. Install dependencies and set up the worktree
After entering the worktree, run the following to bootstrap the environment:

```bash
pnpm install
```

This is required because worktrees share git objects but each needs its own `node_modules`.

### 6b. Copy .env files from the main repo into the worktree
`.env` files are gitignored, so each worktree needs its own copies. After `pnpm install`, copy all `.env` files (excluding `.env.example` files) from the main repo root into the matching relative paths in the worktree.

The main repo root is the working directory you were in before entering the worktree (e.g. `/Users/trang.doan/Desktop/code/discourse-graph`).

Run:
```bash
# From the main repo root, find all .env files (not .env.example) and copy them into the worktree
find . -name ".env*" \
  -not -name ".env.example" \
  -not -path "./.git/*" \
  -not -path "./node_modules/*" \
  -not -path "./.claude/worktrees/*" \
  | while read f; do
      dest=".claude/worktrees/<branch-name>/$f"
      mkdir -p "$(dirname "$dest")"
      cp "$f" "$dest"
    done
```

Report which files were copied so the user can confirm.

### 7. Ask the user which app to start
Ask the user which app they want to run in dev mode. Common options:
- **Roam**: `SUPABASE_USE_DB=none pnpm -C <worktree>/apps/roam dev`
- **Obsidian**: `SUPABASE_USE_DB=local pnpm -C <worktree>/apps/obsidian dev`
- **None**: just set up the environment without starting a dev server

If the user says Roam, also switch the Roam dev symlink:
```bash
ln -sfn <worktree>/apps/roam/dist ~/roam-ext-dev
```
and remind them to reload the developer extension in Roam.

Run the chosen dev command in the background so the user can continue working.

**Dev server gotchas** (learned the hard way — don't rediscover these):

- The filter flag is `--filter`, not `--F`. Turbo 2.5.6 rejects `--F=roam` outright.
- Prefer `pnpm -C <abs-path> <app> dev` over `turbo dev --filter=<app>`. `turbo dev --filter=roam`
  also runs the `@repo/database#dev` dependency, which requires Docker Desktop plus an explicit
  `SUPABASE_USE_DB`; if Docker isn't running turbo fails the *entire* run even though the app
  itself built fine. Going through `pnpm -C` skips the dependency graph.
- `SUPABASE_USE_DB` must be one of `local | branch | production | none | implicit`
  (see `packages/database/src/dbDotEnv.mjs`). Use `none` for work that doesn't touch the database.
- **Always bake the absolute worktree path into the command.** The Bash tool's cwd resets to the
  main repo between calls, so a backgrounded `pnpm --filter roam dev` with no path silently builds
  the *main repo's* `dist` — not the worktree the symlink points at. `pnpm -C <abs-path>` makes the
  path intrinsic to the command so it can't be dropped.
- After starting, verify before reporting success: confirm the log says `built with 0 errors` **and**
  that `<worktree>/apps/roam/dist` has a fresh mtime. A background task that failed still returns a
  task ID.

### 8. Ingest any saved session context
The branch may have been worked on before (e.g. reset from an existing branch).
Check for recorded session context:

```bash
bash ~/.claude/scripts/session-context.sh resolve
```

- If `CONTEXT_EXISTS=yes`, **read the `CONTEXT_FILE`** and load it as working context
  (`Next step`, `Open questions`, `Key decisions`, `Dead ends`).
- If `CONTEXT_EXISTS=no` or the command errors, continue — this is a fresh start.

### 9. Show context
After setup, display:
- Ticket ID and title
- Branch name you're on
- Brief description from the ticket (if available)
- Which app dev server is running (if any)
- If prior session context was found: its `TL;DR` and `Next step`
- A short "ready to work" confirmation
- Remind the user they can run `/checkpoint` to save session context before wrapping up

<result>Findings for tldraw **2.4.6** (source ships in `node_modules`, so all quotes are from real files).

## 1. Version / location

`apps/roam/package.json` pins `"tldraw": "2.4.6"` plus all `@tldraw/*` sub-packages at `2.4.6`. Installed under the app, not the root:
- `/Users/trang.doan/Desktop/code/discourse-graph/.claude/worktrees/eng-2227-add-link-support-to-tldraw-text-shapes-in-roam/apps/roam/node_modules/tldraw/` (has `src/`)
- `.../apps/roam/node_modules/@tldraw/{editor,tlschema,store,validate,...}/src/`

## 2. The `url` prop

Which core shapes declare `url` (all in `.../apps/roam/node_modules/@tldraw/tlschema/src/shapes/`):

| shape | file | validator |
|---|---|---|
| geo | `TLGeoShape.ts:87` | `url: T.linkUrl,` |
| note | `TLNoteShape.ts:43` | `url: T.linkUrl,` |
| image | `TLImageShape.ts:41` | `url: T.linkUrl,` |
| video | `TLVideoShape.ts:27` | `url: T.linkUrl,` |
| bookmark | `TLBookmarkShape.ts:24` | `url: T.linkUrl,` |
| embed | `TLEmbedShape.ts:641` | `url: T.string,` (not `linkUrl`) |

**No `url`:** frame (`frameShapeProps` is only `w`, `h`, `name`), arrow, draw, line, highlight, group, and **text**.

**TLTextShape has no `url` prop in 2.4.6** — `.../@tldraw/tlschema/src/shapes/TLTextShape.ts`:

```ts
export interface TLTextShapeProps {
	color; size; font; textAlign; w: number; text: string; scale: number; autoSize: boolean
}
export const textShapeProps: RecordProps<TLTextShape> = {
	color: DefaultColorStyle, size: DefaultSizeStyle, font: DefaultFontStyle,
	textAlign: DefaultTextAlignStyle, w: T.nonZeroNumber, text: T.string,
	scale: T.nonZeroNumber, autoSize: T.boolean,
}
```
Its migration sequence is at versions 1 (`RemoveJustify`) and 2 (`AddTextAlign`).

`T.linkUrl` is at `.../@tldraw/validate/src/lib/validation.ts:981` — allows `''` and otherwise requires a protocol in `validLinkProtocols`.

## 3. How the built-in link UI decides eligibility

The single gate is a **duck-typed `'url' in shape.props` check**, not a ShapeUtil flag — `.../tldraw/src/lib/ui/hooks/menu-hooks.ts:173`:

```ts
export function useHasLinkShapeSelected() {
	const editor = useEditor()
	return useValue('hasLinkShapeSelected', () => {
		const onlySelectedShape = editor.getOnlySelectedShape()
		return !!(
			onlySelectedShape &&
			onlySelectedShape.type !== 'embed' &&
			'url' in onlySelectedShape.props &&
			!onlySelectedShape.isLocked
		)
	}, [editor])
}
```

Consumers:
- `.../tldraw/src/lib/ui/components/menu-items.tsx:43` `EditLinkMenuItem` — `const shouldDisplay = useHasLinkShapeSelected(); if (!shouldDisplay) return null`
- `.../tldraw/src/lib/ui/components/ActionsMenu/DefaultActionsMenuContent.tsx:138` — `const showEditLink = useHasLinkShapeSelected(); ... disabled={!enabled}`

The action itself (`.../tldraw/src/lib/ui/context/actions.tsx:122`) is unconditional; it just opens the dialog:
```ts
{ id: 'edit-link', label: 'action.edit-link', icon: 'link',
  onSelect(source) { ... editor.mark('edit-link'); addDialog({ component: EditLinkDialog }) } }
```

`EditLinkDialog` re-does the same duck-type check (`.../tldraw/src/lib/ui/components/EditLinkDialog.tsx:36`):
```ts
if (!(selectedShape && 'url' in selectedShape.props && typeof selectedShape.props.url === 'string')) {
	return null
}
```
and writes back generically via `editor.updateShapes([{ id, type, props: { url: urlInputState.safe } }])` (line ~115, and `handleClear` sets `url: ''`). Note the in-file comment: `// ? URL is a magic value`.

**Implication:** adding a `url: T.linkUrl` prop to a custom text shape is sufficient to light up the edit-link menu item and make the dialog work — no other UI wiring is required for that part.

## 4. How the little link icon renders on a shape

There is **no** generic selection-UI link button — each ShapeUtil renders it itself inside `component()` via `HyperlinkButton` (`.../tldraw/src/lib/shapes/shared/HyperlinkButton.tsx`):

```tsx
export function HyperlinkButton({ url, zoomLevel }: { url: string; zoomLevel: number }) {
	return (
		<a className={classNames('tl-hyperlink-button', { 'tl-hyperlink-button__hidden': zoomLevel < 0.32 })}
			href={url} target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer"
			onPointerDown={stopEventPropagation} onPointerUp={stopEventPropagation} ... />
	)
}
```
It is **not exported from `tldraw`'s public index** (it lives in `lib/shapes/shared/`) — check the import path before reusing; it may need to be re-implemented (it's ~25 lines, uses `stopEventPropagation` from `@tldraw/editor` and CSS classes `tl-hyperlink-button` / `tl-hyperlink__icon` already present in `tldraw.css`).

Call sites (all inside the util's `component()` render, wrapped in `HTMLContainer`):
- `.../tldraw/src/lib/shapes/geo/GeoShapeUtil.tsx:469` — `{shape.props.url && <HyperlinkButton url={shape.props.url} zoomLevel={this.editor.getZoomLevel()} />}`
- `NoteShapeUtil.tsx:221`, `ImageShapeUtil.tsx:167` and `:216`, `VideoShapeUtil.tsx:190` — same pattern guarded with `{'url' in shape.props && shape.props.url && ...}`
- `BookmarkShapeUtil.tsx:78`

`TextShapeUtil.component()` (`.../tldraw/src/lib/shapes/text/TextShapeUtil.tsx:71-103`) returns a bare `<TextLabel .../>` with **no** `HTMLContainer` wrapper and no `HyperlinkButton` — so rendering an icon on text requires wrapping/adding it in a subclassed `component()`.

## 5. Extending a core shape's props — supported, with caveats

**Supported.** Only `group` is protected. `.../@tldraw/editor/src/lib/config/defaultShapes.ts`:
```ts
export const coreShapes = [ GroupShapeUtil ] as const
...
if (coreShapeTypes.has(customShape.type)) {
	throw new Error(`Shape type "${customShape.type}" is a core shapes type and cannot be overridden`)
}
if (addedCustomShapeTypes.has(customShape.type)) {
	throw new Error(`Shape type "${customShape.type}" is defined more than once`)
}
```
So a `class MyTextShapeUtil extends TextShapeUtil { static override props = { ...textShapeProps, url: T.linkUrl }; static override migrations = ... }` is fine, **but it must replace `TextShapeUtil` in the `shapeUtils` array** (passing both `TextShapeUtil` and yours throws "defined more than once").

The schema is derived from the utils' statics — `.../@tldraw/editor/src/lib/config/createTLStore.ts:136`:
```ts
function utilsToMap(utils) {
	return Object.fromEntries(utils.map((s) => [s.type, { props: s.props, migrations: s.migrations }]))
}
```

### Migration / validation implications

1. **Validation is strict about both unknown and missing props.** `createShapeValidator` (`.../@tldraw/tlschema/src/shapes/TLBaseShape.ts:34`) does `props: T.object(props)`, and `ObjectValidator` throws on extras (`.../@tldraw/validate/src/lib/validation.ts:302`: `throw new ValidationError('Unexpected property', [key])`) and on a missing/undefined required prop. So persisted text shapes lacking `url` will fail validation on load unless migrated (or unless the validator is `T.linkUrl.optional()` / `.allowUnknownProperties()` is used).

2. **A props migration is the right fix, and it will actually run for `text`.** Add version 3 to the text sequence:
   - The sequence id is forced by `processPropsMigrations` (`.../@tldraw/tlschema/src/recordsWithProps.ts:57`): `` const sequenceId = `com.tldraw.${typeName}.${subType}` `` → `com.tldraw.shape.text`, and there's an `assert(sequenceId === migrations.sequenceId, ...)` if you supply a full sequence object.
   - These library sequences are registered with `retroactive: false` (same file, lines 63/77). That matters for a *brand-new* shape type, but `com.tldraw.shape.text` is already recorded (at version 2) in every persisted tldraw snapshot, so a new `com.tldraw.shape.text/3` migration **will** be applied on load — see `.../@tldraw/store/src/lib/StoreSchema.ts:180-198`, which resolves `theirVersion` and applies everything after it.
   - Danger in the same block: if the persisted version id can't be found in your sequence, you get `return Result.err('Incompatible schema?')`. So keep ids 1 and 2 (`RemoveJustify`, `AddTextAlign`) intact and only append `3: AddUrl` with `up: (props) => { props.url = '' }` and a `down` that deletes it.

3. **Failure mode on load is a hard throw**, not a silent drop — `.../@tldraw/tlschema/src/TLStore.ts:111` `onValidationFailure` annotates and then `throw error` (even in `phase === 'initialize'`; the `isExistingValidationIssue` flag is only an error tag).

4. **Cross-client/read-only concern:** documents written by the extended schema carry `url` on text shapes and record `com.tldraw.shape.text/3`. Any consumer running stock tldraw 2.4.6 (plain `TextShapeUtil`) will hit `'Incompatible schema?'` / `Unexpected property: url` when loading that snapshot. Worth checking whether Roam canvas JSON is ever read by another tldraw instance before committing to this shape.</result>

The tldraw research landed. Key finding, which changes the shape of this ticket:

**`TLTextShape` has no `url` prop in tldraw 2.4.6.** The ticket assumes "reuse the geo-shape link code path," but the eligibility gate is a duck-type check in tldraw itself — `menu-hooks.ts:173` does `'url' in onlySelectedShape.props`. Geo, note, image, video, bookmark declare `url: T.linkUrl`; text, frame, arrow, draw, line do not.

So the work is not UI wiring — it's extending the text shape's schema:

- Subclass `TextShapeUtil` with `static override props = { ...textShapeProps, url: T.linkUrl }` and swap it into `shapeUtils` (passing both throws "defined more than once").
- Append a props migration `com.tldraw.shape.text/3` with `up: props => { props.url = '' }`. Without it, existing persisted text shapes fail validation on load — and the failure is a hard throw, not a silent drop.
- `TextShapeUtil.component()` returns a bare `<TextLabel>` with no `HTMLContainer`, so the link icon needs a wrapper. `HyperlinkButton` is not exported from tldraw's public entry (~25 lines, may need reimplementing).

Two risks worth deciding on before I write the plan: any other tldraw instance reading the same canvas JSON with stock utils will reject `url` on a text shape; and a future tldraw upgrade that adds its own text migration v3 would collide with ours.

The `apps/roam` agent is still mapping the existing geo link path and canvas persistence — I'll fold its findings in and write the plan when it reports.

## 2. Every "link"/"url" occurrence relative to geo shapes — the headline finding

**There is no custom link code in `apps/roam` at all.** The entire "Edit link" feature on geo shapes is 100% stock tldraw 2.4.6. Grep across `src/components/canvas`, `src/utils`, `src/data` for `\blink\b|\burl\b|EditLink|editing-link` returns only unrelated hits:

## 3. How the link value is stored & persisted

**Built-in `url` prop on the shape — no custom meta field.**

`node_modules/.pnpm/@tldraw+tlschema@2.4.6_.../@tldraw/tlschema/src/shapes/TLGeoShape.ts`:
- L65: `url: string` in `TLGeoShapeProps`

Confirmed both blockers directly in the source. Here's the plan.

## What the ticket assumes vs. what's actually there

The ticket says "reuse the geo-shape link code path." There is **no geo link code in `apps/roam`** — the whole feature is stock tldraw 2.4.6, and its eligibility gate is duck-typed:

```
// node_modules/tldraw/src/lib/ui/hooks/menu-hooks.ts:173
'url' in onlySelectedShape.props && !onlySelectedShape.isLocked
```

`geo`, `note`, `image`, `video`, `bookmark` declare `url: T.linkUrl`. `text` does not. So there's nothing to wire up — the work is getting a `url` onto the text shape's schema. `uiOverrides.tsx` already leaves `ContextMenu`, `ActionsMenu` and `Dialogs` at their defaults, so the menu item and `EditLinkDialog` light up for free the moment the prop exists.

## Two blockers I verified

**1. The sync worker validates `text` against stock props.** `apps/tldraw-sync-worker/worker/TldrawDurableObject.ts:19-36` spreads `defaultShapeSchemas` and only adds `{}` entries for *custom* shape types. In `createShapeValidator` ([TLBaseShape.ts:53](apps/tldraw-sync-worker/worker/TldrawDurableObject.ts)) `props ? T.object(props) : T.jsonValue` — so `{}` is fully permissive, but `text` gets the real `textShapeProps` and would reject `url` as `Unexpected property`. Fix is adding `"text"` to the room's `shapeTypes`. Cloud sync is opt-in (`DEFAULT_CANVAS_SYNC_MODE = "local"`), so this only bites sync-mode canvases.

**2. An optional prop won't work.** My first instinct was `T.linkUrl.optional()` to dodge a migration — but the gate is `'url' in props`, which is false when the key is absent. Existing text shapes would silently never show Edit link. So a real migration (`com.tldraw.shape.text/3`, `up: props => { props.url = '' }`) is required, not just nice-to-have.

## The decision worth making before I write code

Both approaches need a `TextShapeUtil` subclass anyway, because `TextShapeUtil.component()` returns a bare `<TextLabel>` with no `HTMLContainer` and no hyperlink button. The difference is where the link lives.

questions.question: Where should the text-shape link be stored?

options.label: url prop + migration (Recommended)
options.description: Subclass TextShapeUtil with props = {...textShapeProps, url: T.linkUrl}, append migration com.tldraw.shape.text/3 backfilling url:'', swap it into shapeUtils, and add "text" to the sync worker's shapeTypes. Faithful to the ticket's 'reuse the geo path' — menu item, EditLinkDialog, translations and analytics all come free. Cost: schema surgery, and a future tldraw upgrade that adds its own text migration v3 would collide.

options.label: shape.meta.url
options.description: Store the link in shape.meta, which createShapeValidator leaves permissive (T.jsonValue) everywhere — no migration, no sync-worker change, no cross-client breakage. Cost: tldraw's built-in gate ignores meta, so we write our own menu item, dialog and write path. This is closer to the 'separate text-shape implementation' the ticket says to avoid.

Confirmed the sites I need to touch. Here's the plan.

## Plan — ENG-2227

### 1. Custom text shape util
New `apps/roam/src/components/canvas/TextShapeWithLinkUtil.tsx`:
- `class TextShapeWithLinkUtil extends TextShapeUtil` with `static override props = { ...textShapeProps, url: T.linkUrl }` and `getDefaultProps()` returning `url: ""`.
- `static override migrations` — the existing `com.tldraw.shape.text` sequence with a version `3` appended, `up: props => { props.url = "" }`, `down` deleting it. Ids 1 (`RemoveJustify`) and 2 (`AddTextAlign`) stay untouched, or `StoreSchema` returns `Incompatible schema?` on load.
- Override `component()` to wrap the base render and append a hyperlink button when `props.url` is set. `HyperlinkButton` is not exported from tldraw's public entry, so reimplement it (~25 lines) reusing the existing `tl-hyperlink-button` / `tl-hyperlink__icon` classes already in `tldraw.css`. `stopEventPropagation` on pointer down/up keeps the click away from the app's shift/ctrl-click handler in [Tldraw.tsx:1396](apps/roam/src/components/canvas/Tldraw.tsx:1396).

### 2. Swap it in at all four assembly sites
`[...defaultShapeUtils, ...customShapeUtils]` appears in [Tldraw.tsx:1342](apps/roam/src/components/canvas/Tldraw.tsx:1342), [useRoamStore.ts:94](apps/roam/src/components/canvas/useRoamStore.ts:94), [TldrawCanvasCloudflareSync.tsx:71](apps/roam/src/components/canvas/TldrawCanvasCloudflareSync.tsx:71) and [Export.tsx:436](apps/roam/src/components/Export.tsx:436). Passing both `TextShapeUtil` and the subclass throws *"defined more than once"*, so add one shared helper that returns `defaultShapeUtils` with `TextShapeUtil` replaced, and use it at all four. They must stay consistent — `Export.tsx` builds a store from persisted data, so a divergent schema there fails validation on export.

### 3. Sync worker
Add `"text"` to the room `shapeTypes` so `createRoomSchema` gives it the permissive `{}` entry instead of stock `textShapeProps`. `mergeSchemaConfig` already unions into existing rooms' stored config, so old rooms pick it up. Note this drops server-side validation of *all* text props, not just `url` — the tradeoff the `{}` mechanism already makes for every custom shape.

### 4. Tests
`vitest.config.mts` only collects `src/utils/__tests__/**` in a `node` environment, so component tests won't run. I'll put the pure logic in `src/utils/textShapeLink.ts` (eligibility predicate + the migration's `up`/`down`) and test in `src/utils/__tests__/textShapeLink.test.ts`:
- migration `up` backfills `url: ""` on a v2 text shape; `down` removes it
- a migrated text shape satisfies `'url' in props` (the actual gate) — this is the "eligibility" case, and it's what catches the optional-prop trap
- round-trip through the store serialize/load path used by `useRoamStore`, mirroring `migratePropsStoreDefault.test.ts`

### 5. Verification
`pnpm -C apps/roam test:unit`, then manual in Roam: add a link to a text shape, close and reopen the canvas, confirm it persists and the icon opens the target. Then `pnpm ci:validate` from the root before the PR.

### Risk to flag in the PR
A future tldraw upgrade that adds its own `com.tldraw.shape.text` version 3 collides with ours. I'll put a one-line comment at the migration naming the constraint.

Want me to start implementing, or look anything over first?
we need to set the versioning for this and migrate at all or no? what would happen to the older text shape?
Good question — and the honest answer is I shouldn't guess at it. Let me read the exact validation and migration paths.

content.text:
Yes — versioning and a migration are both required. I ran it rather than reasoned about it; here's what actually happens.

## What happens to older text shapes

I built the three cases against real tldraw 2.4.6 schemas (throwaway test, now deleted): a stock-schema text shape serialized, then loaded by an extended schema.

**A — extended schema, no migration:**
```
A migrate result: success
A props after migrate: {...,"autoSize":true}     ← no url
A 'url' in props: false
A validate error: At shape(type = text).props.url: Expected string, got undefined
```
The migration step reports success and silently does nothing, then **validation throws**. `ObjectValidator` calls every configured validator with `getOwnProperty(object, key)`, so a missing key reaches `T.linkUrl` as `undefined`. And `onValidationFailure` ([TLStore.ts:134](apps/roam/src/components/canvas/useRoamStore.ts)) ends in a bare `throw error` — the `phase === 'initialize'` branch only tags the error, it doesn't swallow it.

So without a migration, **every existing canvas containing a text shape fails to open.** Not a silent degrade — a hard throw.

This also kills the `.optional()` shortcut I was considering. Even if optional made validation pass, the gate is `'url' in props`, which is `false` above — so old text shapes would never show Edit link while new ones would. Silent inconsistency is worse than the throw.

**B — with the migration:** `url` backfilled to `""`, validation clean.

**C — a stock-schema client reading our document:** `At shape(type = text).props.url: Unexpected property`. This is the sync worker case, confirming it needs `"text"` added to its `shapeTypes`.

## Where the version should live — this changes my earlier recommendation

I'd said append `com.tldraw.shape.text/3` and flagged upstream collision as a risk. There's a better option: **the repo already owns a migration sequence.** [discourseRelationMigrations.ts:52](apps/roam/src/components/canvas/DiscourseRelationShape/discourseRelationMigrations.ts:52) defines `com.roam-research.discourse-graphs`, currently at version 5, with `scope: "store"` migrations. Add version 6 there instead:

- No collision with upstream — a future tldraw bumping `com.tldraw.shape.text` to 3 can't clash with our namespace.
- `createMigrationSequence` defaults `retroactive = true` ([migrate.ts:72](apps/roam/src/components/canvas/DiscourseRelationShape/discourseRelationMigrations.ts)), so it applies to documents that predate the sequence, not just ones already carrying it.
- All four store-creation sites already thread `migrations` through ([useRoamStore.ts:93](apps/roam/src/components/canvas/useRoamStore.ts:93), [TldrawCanvasCloudflareSync.tsx:95](apps/roam/src/components/canvas/TldrawCanvasCloudflareSync.tsx:95), [Export.tsx:432](apps/roam/src/components/Export.tsx:432)), so there's no new plumbing.

Test B used exactly this shape — repo sequence, `scope: "store"`, version 6 — and it works.

One constraint the experiment surfaced: `validateMigrations` rejects a sequence that doesn't start at 1, so 6 must be *appended* to the existing 1–5, never split into its own file.

Want me to implement it this way?

So let's say we have a text created before this code change. And I just want to make it so smooth that they don't have to think about a migration, but they can still attach an URL to a text shape. What is the best path for us to do this?
That reframes it well — a migration is invisible *when it works*; the pain is its failure mode. Let me check whether there's a path with no migration at all.

content.text:
Best path: **store the link in `shape.meta.url`, not in props.** No migration, no version, nothing for a user to think about — and critically, no failure mode if anything is out of step.

## Why this is the smooth one

I verified each claim against the real schemas:

**Old text shapes need nothing.** tldraw already guarantees `meta` exists on every shape — `AddMeta` is version 3 of its own `com.tldraw.shape` root sequence ([TLShape.ts:123](apps/roam/src/components/canvas/DiscourseRelationShape/discourseRelationMigrations.ts)), applied to every persisted document years ago. A pre-change text shape arrives with `meta: {}`, which simply means "no link." Absence is a valid state, so there's nothing to backfill.

**Meta is unvalidated by design.** `createShapeValidator` does `meta: meta ? T.object(meta) : T.jsonValue` — and no default shape declares a meta schema. Tested:
```
STOCK + meta.url:                    none      ← stock tldraw accepts it
STOCK + empty meta (pre-change):     none
round-trip:  success  {"url":"https://example.com"}
```
That first line is the whole argument. The **stock** schema validates a text shape carrying `meta.url` without complaint — so the sync worker needs no change, and a user who rolls the extension back still opens their canvas fine; the link is just ignored, not fatal.

Compare the props route, which I also measured: no migration → `Expected string, got undefined`, thrown, canvas won't open. With a migration it works, but you're permanently coordinating a version number across the client, the sync worker's room schema, and every persisted document. That's the thing you don't want users (or us) thinking about.

## What it costs

tldraw's built-in gate is `'url' in shape.props`, so meta doesn't light up the stock Edit link item — we write that part. The app already has every pattern for it:

1. **Menu item** — `CustomContextMenu` already appends `TldrawUiMenuGroup`/`TldrawUiMenuItem` groups at [uiOverrides.tsx:461-514](apps/roam/src/components/canvas/uiOverrides.tsx:461). One more group, shown when `selectedShape?.type === "text"` — the same shape-type gating already used for Convert To at [uiOverrides.tsx:437](apps/roam/src/components/canvas/uiOverrides.tsx:437).
2. **Dialog** — `TldrawUiDialogHeader/Body/Footer`, `TldrawUiInput` and `useDialogs` are all publicly exported, so it looks identical to the geo dialog rather than merely similar. Reuse tldraw's `validateUrl` logic (auto-prefix `https://`, `T.linkUrl`).
3. **Hyperlink button** — needed either way, since `TextShapeUtil.component()` returns a bare `<TextLabel>` with no `HTMLContainer`. ~25 lines reusing the existing `tl-hyperlink-button` CSS.

A side benefit for the ticket's test requirement: eligibility and the read/write helpers become pure app functions in `src/utils/`, which is the only place `vitest.config.mts` collects from. The props route would have put the interesting logic in a migration inside a component file.

## The one thing to flag

The ticket says "reuse the geo-shape link code path instead of creating a separate text-shape implementation." This is deliberately the opposite, and that line was written assuming the geo path was app code we could share — it isn't, it's stock tldraw gated on a prop text doesn't have. I'd note that on the ticket so the author can push back, since the visible result is the same but the reasoning changed.

The tradeoff in one line: **props** = free UI, permanent migration burden; **meta** = ~150 lines of UI we already have patterns for, zero migration burden forever.

content.text:
Yes — there's a clear precedent, and it does support the props approach. That changes my recommendation.

## The history

One sequence, `com.roam-research.discourse-graphs`, defined in [discourseRelationMigrations.ts:52](apps/roam/src/components/canvas/DiscourseRelationShape/discourseRelationMigrations.ts:52), currently at version 5:

| v | id | what it does |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `ExtractBindings` | store-scope restructure |
| 2 | `"2.3.0"` | **adds** `start`, `end`, `labelPosition`, `scale`, `color`, `labelColor` |
| 3 | `AddSizeAndFontFamily` | **adds** `size`, `fontFamily` |
| 4 | `RemoveNullAssetFileSize` | deletes a bad prop |
| 5 | `MigrateNodeTypeToDiscourseNode` | **adds** `nodeTypeId`, rewrites `shape.type` |

Three of the five are exactly "add a prop to a shape, bump the version." Shipped in `f575944a5`, `cce0ff1d9`. So adding `url` as version 6 is squarely in-pattern, not a new mechanism.

The idempotency detail is worth copying too — v3 originally did `shape.props.size = "m"` unconditionally and had to be fixed in `e0710ec4b` ("don't enforce font style and size on migration", your own PR #916) to `if (!shape.props.size)`. A `url` migration should be written defensively the same way: `if (shape.props.url === undefined) shape.props.url = ""`.

## What the precedent doesn't cover

All five migrations act on shapes the app owns — `discourse-node`, relation shapes, referenced-node shapes. [useCanvasStoreAdapterArgs.ts:72-79](apps/roam/src/components/canvas/useCanvasStoreAdapterArgs.ts:72) registers only custom utils; **no default tldraw shape util is overridden anywhere today.** `text` would be the first. That brings two things the pattern has never had to handle: replacing `TextShapeUtil` consistently at all four store-creation sites, and the sync worker, which validates `text` against stock `textShapeProps` and would reject `url` until `"text"` is added to its `shapeTypes`.

## Correcting my earlier lean

I oversold meta's safety on one point. I implied a downgrade would be newly fatal with props — but `getMigrationsSince` returns `Result.err('Incompatible schema?')` whenever the persisted version isn't in the installed sequence ([StoreSchema.ts:193](apps/roam/src/components/canvas/useCanvasStoreAdapterArgs.ts)). Any canvas already migrated to v5 breaks the same way on an older extension today. That risk is inherent to the existing pattern, not something `url` introduces.

With that corrected, the ledger tips: **go with the `url` prop at version 6.** It matches the ticket's "reuse the geo-shape code path", matches the codebase's own migration pattern, and gives you the Edit link menu item, dialog and translations for free. For a user with a pre-existing text shape the migration is invisible — `retroactive` defaults to true, so it backfills `url: ""` on load and the shape immediately shows Edit link.

Meta remains the right call only if we wanted text links to survive an extension rollback, and the codebase has already decided that's not a constraint it holds.

## Revised plan

1. `TextShapeWithLinkUtil extends TextShapeUtil` — `props = { ...textShapeProps, url: T.linkUrl }`, `getDefaultProps` with `url: ""`, `component()` wrapped to render the hyperlink button.
2. Version 6 `AddTextShapeUrl` appended to the existing sequence, `scope: "record"`, filtered to `typeName === "shape" && type === "text"`, defensive `up`. That file's header TODO already says to rename it `discourseMigrations.ts` since it's no longer relation-only — this makes the case stronger; I'd do the rename.
3. Swap the util in at all four sites via one shared helper.
4. Add `"text"` to the sync worker's `shapeTypes`.
5. Tests in `src/utils/` covering the migration `up` (including idempotency, the v3 bug) and that a migrated shape satisfies `'url' in props`.

content.text:
Implemented and verified as far as static checks go.

## What's in the change

| File | What |
|---|---|
| `TextShapeWithLinkUtil.tsx` *(new)* | `extends TextShapeUtil` with `props = { ...textShapeProps, url: T.linkUrl }`, `getDefaultProps` returning `url: ""`, and `component()` wrapped to render the link icon |
| `baseShapeUtils.ts` *(new)* | `defaultShapeUtils` with `TextShapeUtil` swapped out — tldraw throws if a type registers twice |
| `discourseRelationMigrations.ts` | version 6 `AddTextShapeUrl`, `scope: "record"`, filtered to text shapes |
| `textShapeLink.ts` + tests *(new)* | pure predicates and the backfill, where `vitest.config.mts` can actually collect them |
| `Export.tsx`, `Tldraw.tsx`, `useRoamStore.ts`, `TldrawCanvasCloudflareSync.tsx` | use `baseShapeUtils`; sync client now declares `"text"` to the worker |

I reimplemented `HyperlinkButton` (~25 lines) since tldraw doesn't export it, matching its markup so text links look identical to geo links. Two casts were needed in the util — the tree has two React type copies, so `TextShapeUtil.component`'s declared `JSX.Element` is nominally distinct from ours (`key` is `Key | null` vs `string | null`). It's commented.

The migration copies the lesson from your PR #916: `backfillTextShapeUrl` only writes when `url === undefined`, and there's a test asserting two applications don't clobber a user's value.

## Verification

- `pnpm check-types` — clean
- `pnpm test:unit` — 233 passed, 36 files (7 new)
- `pnpm build` — `built with 0 errors`; confirmed `AddTextShapeUrl` and `tl-hyperlink-button` are actually in `dist/extension.js`
- Lint — 0 errors. Since CI's `lint-changed-files` fails on *warnings* for added lines, I diffed the migration file's warnings against its pre-change state: identical three, all on pre-existing lines (one just shifted 90→95 from my import). No new warnings on added lines.

Two tests encode the behaviour we reasoned about: an unmigrated pre-link text shape throws on validation, and a migrated one satisfies `'url' in props` — the exact gate `useHasLinkShapeSelected` uses.

## Not verified

I haven't opened this in Roam. The menu item appearing under Edit ▸, the icon rendering top-right, and persistence across a canvas close/reopen are all things only the real app can confirm — and the ticket's Done When calls for that persistence check explicitly. You declined the dev server at setup; say the word and I'll point `~/roam-ext-dev` at this worktree and start the watcher so you can reload and check. (Worth noting `~/roam-ext-dev` is shared across worktree sessions, so I'd verify its target first.)

Changes are staged but uncommitted.

Persist the **reasoning layer** of this work session (goal, decisions, dead ends,
constraints, next step) to the Obsidian vault, keyed to the current worktree.
Files are plain markdown written directly — no MCP, no Obsidian required running.

## Steps

### 1. Resolve where to write
Run the helper from the current worktree:

```bash
bash ~/.claude/scripts/session-context.sh resolve
```

It prints `TICKET`, `BRANCH`, `WORKTREE`, `SESSION_DIR`, `CONTEXT_FILE`,
`LOG_FILE`, `STAMP`, `CONTEXT_EXISTS` and creates the folders. **Only write to the
`CONTEXT_FILE` and `LOG_FILE` paths it gives you** — never elsewhere in the vault.
If it errors (not a git repo / detached HEAD), tell the user and stop.

### 2. Read existing context if present
If `CONTEXT_EXISTS=yes`, read `CONTEXT_FILE` first so you UPDATE it rather than
overwrite history. Digest sections get rewritten; accreting sections get appended.

### 3. Gather the reasoning layer
Reconstruct from this session's conversation + git. If a ticket id is present and
Linear is available, you may fetch the title/URL with `mcp__linear-server__get_issue`.
Apply the **extraction rubric** below to decide what is worth recording.

### 4. Write `_context.md`
Use the template at `~/.claude/skills/checkpoint/template.md` as the structure.
- If new file: fill the template. Set `created`/`updated` to today, `sessions: 1`.
- If updating: rewrite digest sections (TL;DR, Current state, Next step, Open
  questions, key_files, status), **append** to accreting sections (Key decisions,
  Dead ends, Constraints, Gotchas) with a dated bullet, bump `updated` to today
  and increment `sessions`.

### 5. Append a log snapshot
Write a short dated entry to `LOG_FILE` (a fresh file — no append needed):
a 3–6 line summary of what THIS session accomplished + what changed since last time.
This is the immutable audit trail; `_context.md` is the living digest.

### 6. Confirm
Tell the user what you wrote (context file + log file paths) and the one-line Next step.

## Extraction rubric — what to record (keep it concise)

**The test:** record a line only if it would otherwise have to be *re-derived* or
would prevent *repeating a mistake*. Ask: *"What do I know now that I didn't at
session start, that isn't already in Linear, git, or the code?"*

**DO record (the reasoning layer — it evaporates when the session ends):**
- Scope agreement: how the ticket was interpreted, what's in/out of scope.
- Decisions: what + why + what was rejected + what would make us revisit it.
- Dead ends: what was tried that failed, and why.
- Constraints/preferences the user stated ("ship by Fri", "don't touch billing").
- Gotchas: environmental facts learned the hard way.
- Next step + open questions + current status.

**Do NOT record (noise / lives elsewhere):**
- Activity logs ("edited foo.ts, ran tests") — record outcomes, not keystrokes.
- Anything copy-pasteable from the diff, git history, or the Linear ticket body.
- Resolved questions — delete them or fold the answer into a decision.
- Restating how the code works — that's what the code is for.

**Mark uncertainty** explicitly (`*assumed*`, `*unchecked*`). Prefer 8 sharp lines
over 40 vague ones — this must stay skimmable for the user, not just parseable by an agent.

> **TL;DR** Code is written and statically verified (types, 233 tests, build, bundle grep) but has never been opened in Roam. The ticket's premise was wrong — there is no app-side geo link code to reuse; the real work was giving the text shape a `url` prop plus a migration.

## Goal / scope agreement
Ticket said "reuse the geo-shape link code path." There is no such code in `apps/roam` — the entire geo link feature is stock tldraw 2.4.6, gated on a duck-type check `'url' in shape.props` (`menu-hooks.ts:173`). `text` has no `url` prop, so the work is schema, not UI wiring. Once the prop exists, the context-menu item and `EditLinkDialog` light up for free because `uiOverrides.tsx` leaves `ContextMenu`, `ActionsMenu` and `Dialogs` at defaults.

## Key decisions
- **[2026-09-14] Store the link in `shape.props.url`, not `shape.meta`** — *Why:* matches the ticket, and the codebase already has a props-migration pattern (3 of the 5 existing migrations add props to shapes). *Rejected:* `shape.meta.url`, which needs no migration at all because `createShapeValidator` leaves meta as `T.jsonValue` — but it requires hand-rolling the menu item + dialog, i.e. exactly the "separate text-shape implementation" the ticket forbids. *Revisit if:* we ever need text links to survive an extension rollback.
- **[2026-09-14] Put the migration in `com.roam-research.discourse-graphs` v6, not `com.tldraw.shape.text` v3** — *Why:* our own namespace can't collide with a future tldraw release that bumps its text sequence. *Revisit if:* the sequence is ever split per shape type.
- **[2026-09-14] Backfill defensively (`if url === undefined`)** — *Why:* migration v3 originally assigned unconditionally and clobbered user values; fixed in PR #916 (your own). A test asserts double-application is a no-op.

## Dead ends
- `T.linkUrl.optional()` to avoid writing a migration — looked like it would work, but the eligibility gate is `'url' in props`, which is false when the key is absent. Old text shapes would silently never show Edit link while new ones would. A migration is mandatory, not a nicety.
- Reasoning about what happens to un-migrated shapes — had to be measured. Without the migration, `migrateStoreSnapshot` reports **success** and silently does nothing, then validation throws `At shape(type = text).props.url: Expected string, got undefined`, and `onValidationFailure` rethrows even at `phase === 'initialize'`. Failure mode is "canvas won't open", not a silent degrade.
- Importing tldraw's CJS bundle in `node -e` to check exports — hangs (pulls in React/DOM). Grep the `.d.ts` or copy an existing import from `DiscourseNodeUtil.tsx` instead.

## Constraints & preferences
- No dev server this session — user asked to go straight to planning, so nothing has been exercised in the real app.
- User pushed back twice on my recommendations and was right both times; the props-vs-meta call was only settled by looking at actual repo history rather than arguing from first principles.

## Gotchas / landmines
- The sync worker (`apps/tldraw-sync-worker/worker/TldrawDurableObject.ts`) builds its room schema from `defaultShapeSchemas` + `{}` entries for custom types. `{}` is fully permissive (`props ? T.object(props) : T.jsonValue`), but `text` gets real `textShapeProps` and would reject `url` — hence `"text"` is now appended to the `shapeType` query params in `TldrawCanvasCloudflareSync.tsx`. Side effect: server-side validation of *all* text props is now off.
- `[...defaultShapeUtils, ...customShapeUtils]` appears at **four** sites (`Tldraw.tsx`, `useRoamStore.ts`, `TldrawCanvasCloudflareSync.tsx`, `Export.tsx`). They must stay in sync or `Export.tsx` fails validating persisted data. Hence `baseShapeUtils.ts`.
- Registering both `TextShapeUtil` and a subclass throws *"defined more than once"* — it must be replaced in the list, not appended.
- Two React type copies in the tree: `TextShapeUtil.component`'s declared `JSX.Element` is nominally distinct from ours (`key` is `Key | null` vs `string | null`). Needs a cast; commented in the file.
- `createMigrationSequence` rejects a sequence that doesn't start at version 1 — v6 must be appended in place, never split into its own file.
- Downgrading the extension already breaks any canvas migrated past the installed version (`getMigrationsSince` → `Result.err('Incompatible schema?')`). This predates our change; don't treat it as newly introduced.
- `vitest.config.mts` only collects `src/utils/__tests__/**` in a `node` environment — component tests are silently not run. Pure logic has to live in `src/utils/` to be testable.

## Current state
All code written, staged, uncommitted. `pnpm check-types` clean, `pnpm test:unit` 233 passed (7 new), `pnpm build` 0 errors with `AddTextShapeUrl` and `tl-hyperlink-button` confirmed present in `dist/extension.js`. Lint has 0 errors and no *new* warnings on added lines (verified by diffing the migration file's warnings against its pre-change state — CI's `lint-changed-files` fails on warnings for added lines).

## Next step
Open it in Roam and confirm the three things static checks can't: Edit link appears under Edit ▸ for a text shape, the icon renders top-right and opens the target, and the link survives closing and reopening the canvas (the ticket's Done When calls that out explicitly). Point `~/roam-ext-dev` at this worktree first — it is shared across worktree sessions, so check its current target before trusting a reload.

## Open questions / blockers
- Should the ticket be updated to note that "reuse the geo-shape link code path" was based on a wrong premise? Worth a comment to Michael so the change isn't read as ignoring the instruction.
- Turning off server-side validation for text props in sync mode is a real (if small) tradeoff nobody has explicitly signed off on. *unchecked* whether anyone is actually using cloud sync yet — `DEFAULT_CANVAS_SYNC_MODE` is `local`.
EOF

<result>Typecheck and the new unit tests pass. Here are my findings.

## 1. CRITICAL — adding `"text"` to the sync room's `shapeType` list breaks the Cloudflare sync worker entirely

`apps/roam/src/components/canvas/TldrawCanvasCloudflareSync.tsx:83` now sends `shapeType=text` to the worker. The worker turns each declared shape type into an **empty** schema entry (`apps/tldraw-sync-worker/worker/TldrawDurableObject.ts:20-24`: `Object.fromEntries(shapeTypes.map((type) => [type, {}]))`), which overwrites `defaultShapeSchemas.text`. That drops not just the props validator (intended) but also `textShapeMigrations`.

`processPropsMigrations` (tlschema 2.4.6 `recordsWithProps.ts:58-66`) still registers the sequence id `com.tldraw.shape.text`, but with an **empty** sequence — server version `0`, while every client reports version `2` (`RemoveJustify`, `AddTextAlign`). `StoreSchema.getMigrationsSince` then does `findIndex(m => m.id === 'com.tldraw.shape.text/2')` on an empty array, gets `-1`, and returns `Result.err('Incompatible schema?')` (`@tldraw/store/src/lib/StoreSchema.ts:190-193`).

Reproduced against the installed 2.4.6 packages:

```
client text seq: 2
server text seq: 0
getMigrationsSince ok? false  Incompatible schema?
```

Two concrete failures:

- **Every client is rejected on connect.** `TLSyncRoom.handleConnectRequest` (`@tldraw/sync-core/src/lib/TLSyncRoom.ts:701-705`) calls `getMigrationsSince(message.schema)`; on `!migrations.ok` it calls `rejectSession(..., TLIncompatibilityReason.ClientTooOld)`. Scenario: user opens any canvas with `canvasSyncMode === "sync"` → worker merges `"text"` into the stored config → the socket is closed immediately with "client too old". This hits clients *with* this change and clients *without* it equally.
- **Existing rooms fail to load at all.** `TLSyncRoom`'s constructor calls `this.schema.migrateStoreSnapshot({ store, schema: snapshot.schema })` (`TLSyncRoom.ts:299-310`) and `throw new Error('Failed to migrate: ' + reason)` on error. Every R2 room snapshot persisted so far carries `com.tldraw.shape.text: 2`, so `createRoom` throws and `/connect/:roomId` 500s.

Aggravating factor: `ensureSchemaConfig` (`TldrawDurableObject.ts:161-181`) **persists** the merged config to Durable Object storage. Once one client on this build touches a room, `"text"` is in that room's config permanently — rolling back the extension does not un-break the room; the stored `schemaConfig` has to be cleared manually.

Fix direction: the worker must not blank out a default shape type. Special-case it, e.g. `text: { migrations: defaultShapeSchemas.text.migrations, props: { ...textShapeProps, url: T.linkUrl } }`, and ship the worker change with (or before) the client change. The `{}` trick is only safe for types the *client* also registers with no migrations, which is why it works for the discourse node/relation types today (both sides at version 0).

## 2. Class-name bug in the copied `HyperlinkButton` — the hide-at-low-zoom behavior is inverted into a broken class

`apps/roam/src/components/canvas/TextShapeWithLinkUtil.tsx:22-24`:

```tsx
className={`tl-hyperlink-button${
  zoomLevel < 0.32 ? "tl-hyperlink-button__hidden" : ""
}`}
```

tldraw uses `classNames(...)` (`tldraw/src/lib/shapes/shared/HyperlinkButton.tsx:10-12`), which emits `"tl-hyperlink-button tl-hyperlink-button__hidden"` — space-separated. The template literal here concatenates with no space, producing the single token `tl-hyperlink-buttontl-hyperlink-button__hidden`, which matches neither rule.

Failure scenario: zoom below 32%. Instead of `display: none` (`tldraw.css:1084`), the anchor loses `.tl-hyperlink-button` too, so it renders unstyled and un-positioned (no `position: absolute; top:0; right:0`) — a stray clickable link near the shape origin, still `pointer-events: all`, on every linked text shape. Geo shapes hide correctly, so text links visibly diverge from geo at low zoom — the opposite of the stated goal.

## 3. Old extension versions can no longer open a canvas that has been opened by this build

Not a defect in the change so much as a rollout hazard worth naming, since Roam graphs are shared and extension versions are not uniform.

- An old client's schema has `com.roam-research.discourse-graphs` at 5. Loading a snapshot stamped 6 makes `getMigrationsSince` look for `.../6` in a sequence that ends at 5 → `-1` → `'Incompatible schema?'` → `loadSnapshot` fails and `useRoamStore` reports "Failed to migrate snapshot" (`apps/roam/src/components/canvas/useRoamStore.ts:274-280`), i.e. the canvas will not open.
- Even past that, the extra prop is rejected outright. Verified against a stock 2.4.6 schema: `At shape(type = text).props.url: Unexpected property`.

There is no down-path for a user who rolls back, and `down` on migration v6 only runs if something actually invokes a downgrade. Worth a release note at minimum.

## Categories where I found nothing

**`baseShapeUtils` coverage (category 1) — complete for apps/roam.** All four client store/editor sites use it: `Export.tsx:436`, `Tldraw.tsx:1342`, `TldrawCanvasCloudflareSync.tsx:71`, `useRoamStore.ts:94`. No remaining `defaultShapeUtils` reference in `apps/roam`. `canvasSyncMode.ts`'s local→cloud migration goes through `getRoamCanvasSnapshot` → `createCanvasStore`, so it inherits the right list. `apps/obsidian` uses its own tldraw 3.14.2 and a separate store — unaffected. The one remaining schema construction site is the sync worker, which is finding #1.

**Programmatic text-shape creation (category 2) — nothing broken.** `defaultHandleExternalTextContent.ts:142-153` passes a *partial* props object to `editor.createShapes`, and tldraw fills the rest from `getDefaultProps()`, which now includes `url: ""`. `Clipboard.tsx:747`, `uiOverrides.tsx:204`, `DiscourseNodeUtil.tsx`, `DiscourseToolPanel.tsx`, `overlays/relationCreation.ts`, `DiscourseRelationTool.tsx` all create discourse node/relation shapes, not text. The only place a *complete* shape record is hand-built and written straight into a store snapshot is `Export.tsx:592-612`, and that's a `DiscourseNodeShape`. No `updateShapes` call writes a whole text props object. Minor UX note only: Convert To (`uiOverrides.tsx:243-248`) reads `props.text` and discards the `url` when replacing the text shape with a discourse node.

**Migration reachability (category 3) — v6 is reachable, but the legacy fixtures contain no text shapes.** `LEGACY_SCHEMA` is `schemaVersion: 1`, so `upgradeSchema` maps it to sequence ids without `com.roam-research.discourse-graphs`; `createMigrationSequence` defaults `retroactive: true` (`@tldraw/store/src/lib/migrate.ts:114`), so `getMigrationsSince` adds the whole roam sequence including v6 (`StoreSchema.ts:168-173`). Snapshots already at v5 pick up v6 via the normal `slice(idx + 1)` path. For reference: `apps/roam/src/data/legacyTldrawSchema.ts` has `text: 0` in `subTypeVersions` but `LEGACY_STORE_TEST` contains **no** `type: "text"` record, so the legacy fixture exercises nothing about this migration.

**`component()` override (category 4) — no breakage found.** Hook ordering is safe: `super.component(shape)` is called unconditionally and first, so `useDefaultColorTheme()` / `useTextShapeKeydownHandler()` run in a fixed order regardless of `url`; `getZoomLevel()` is not a hook and is only read when `url` is truthy (inside the `&&`), so only linked shapes re-render on zoom — same as `GeoShapeUtil.tsx:469-471`. Shift/ctrl-click node-opening (`Tldraw.tsx:1397-1401`) early-returns on `!isDiscourseNodeShape`, so text shapes are unaffected. `edit-link` remains reachable via `DefaultContextMenuContent` (`menu-items.tsx:41-44`) and the actions menu, both gated on `useHasLinkShapeSelected`, whose `'url' in props` check the new prop satisfies.

- `apps/roam/src/utils/textShapeLink.ts:8-10` — `isTextShapeRecord` accepts `props === null` (`typeof null === "object"`), and `backfillTextShapeUrl:24` then dereferences `props.url`, throwing inside the migration. `hasLinkUrlProp:16` guards null but `isTextShapeRecord` does not. Not reachable with real tldraw records, but the inconsistency means a corrupt record turns a canvas-open into an unhandled migration error rather than a skip.
- `apps/roam/src/components/canvas/baseShapeUtils.ts:10-13` fails silently if `util === TextShapeUtil` ever stops matching by identity (a second tldraw copy in the graph, or an import from a different entry point). The result would be a store whose schema lacks `url` while the UI still writes it — validation failures on save rather than a loud error. An `assert` that the map replaced exactly one entry would make that loud.
- `apps/roam/src/utils/__tests__/textShapeLink.test.ts:80-91` builds a *hand-rolled* schema (`defaultShapeSchemas.text` + `geo.props.url`) rather than deriving one from `TextShapeWithLinkUtil` / `baseShapeUtils`, and never runs the real `createMigrations` sequence. # DG Roam Playwright Session

Use this skill to open a real Roam Research graph once, run all checks in the returned context, capture proof, and close it cleanly.

Secrets must live only in the ignored `apps/roam/.env`. Do not print, inspect, or commit passwords, cookies, local storage, or Playwright profile contents.

## Quick Start

Open slot 1:

```sh
pnpm --filter roam playwright:open -- --slot 1
```

Use slots 2 or 3 for isolated concurrent work:

```sh
pnpm --filter roam playwright:open -- --slot 2
pnpm --filter roam playwright:open -- --slot 3
```

The script writes screenshots and JSON proof under `local/roam-playwright/artifacts`.

For loading `apps/roam/dist` and running a feature test in the same context, use `dg-roam-load-extension` instead of creating a temporary browser harness.

## Environment

The ignored `apps/roam/.env` should contain one set per slot:

```sh
DG_ROAM_PLAYWRIGHT_EMAIL_1=
DG_ROAM_PLAYWRIGHT_PASSWORD_1=
DG_ROAM_PLAYWRIGHT_GRAPH_URL_1=
DG_ROAM_PLAYWRIGHT_PROFILE_DIR_1=
```

Repeat for `_2` and `_3`.

Account emails and graph URLs are intentionally required from the ignored app `.env`. Do not add real test account identifiers, graph names, graph URLs, or passwords to committed files.

Profile directories default to ignored local paths under `local/roam-playwright/profiles/`.

The repo-relative `.env`, profile, and artifact paths work on Windows and macOS. Override them only when the slot needs a different local location:

- `DG_ROAM_PLAYWRIGHT_ENV_PATH`: alternate ignored environment file.
- `DG_ROAM_PLAYWRIGHT_PROFILE_DIR_<slot>` or `--profile-dir`: slot profile.
- `--out`: proof output directory.

When importing `openRoamSession`, keep the returned session and call `session.close()` in `finally`. A failed navigation or readiness check closes the context automatically.

## Safety Notes

- Only one Chromium process can own a persistent profile at a time.
- A profile-lock error identifies the occupied slot and path. Close that session or use another `--slot`; do not delete lock files.
- Use `--headed --allow-login` if manual login recovery is needed.
- Credential values never belong in result JSON or diagnostics.
- Do not run Supabase smoke tests as part of this skill; this skill is only for Roam login/session proof.

# DG Roam Load Extension

Use this skill for one complete lifecycle: build `apps/roam`, open an authenticated slot, register `apps/roam/dist`, activate it, verify DG runtime readiness, run an optional caller test, capture proof, and close.

It composes with `dg-roam-playwright-session` for account/profile selection.

## Quick Start

```sh
pnpm --filter roam playwright:load-extension -- --slot 1
```

Use another slot for isolated work:

```sh
pnpm --filter roam playwright:load-extension -- --slot 2
```

The script builds by default, verifies `window.roamjs.extension.queryBuilder`, checks the DG settings UI, and writes proof under `local/roam-playwright/artifacts`.

To add feature-specific assertions without copying the loader, pass an ESM test module:

```sh
pnpm --filter roam playwright:load-extension -- --slot 1 --test-module ./local/roam-playwright/feature-proof.mjs
```

```js
export default {
  readySelector: "[data-testid='feature-ready']",
  async ready({ page }) {
    return page.evaluate(() => Boolean(window.myFeature?.ready));
  },
  async run({ page, outDir }) {
    await page.getByText("Expected output").waitFor();
    return { assertion: "passed" };
  },
  async cleanup({ page, state }) {
    // Remove only fixtures created by run().
  },
};
```

`run()` starts only after the standard DG runtime proof and any caller readiness hook succeeds. `cleanup()` runs when `run()` started, including after a failed assertion. Return JSON-serializable proof values.

## Options

- `--slot 1|2|3`: Select the Roam account/profile.
- `--skip-build`: Load the existing `apps/roam/dist` without rebuilding.
- `--headed`: Run with a visible Chromium window.
- `--keep-open`: Leave the browser open after loading.
- `--dist <path>`: Load a different Roam extension folder. Use only when intentionally testing another build output.
- `--registration-name <name>`: Developer Extensions row name. Defaults to the built folder name, usually `dist`.
- `--test-module <path>`: Caller readiness, test, and cleanup hooks. Absolute Windows paths and paths containing spaces are supported.
- `--out <path>` and `--screenshot-name <name>`: Proof artifact locations.
- `--timeout <ms>`: UI and readiness timeout. Defaults to `45000`.

content.text:
Fixes pushed and the PR body updated. Two things to report.

**The icon.** You were right that it felt cramped, and the cause is structural: I copied geo's placement (`top:0; right:0`, inside the shape), but a geo shape is a box with empty corner space while a text shape's bounds hug the glyphs — so the 44px button lands on the last word. It now sits just outside the right edge, vertically centred, via a `dg-text-link-button` class in `tldrawStyles.ts`. `.tl-shape` is `overflow: visible`, so nothing clips it.

**The review found a release-blocking bug in my own work.** Declaring `"text"` to the sync worker the way custom shape types are declared blanks its schema entry to `{}` — which also drops `textShapeMigrations`. I reproduced it:

```
client text seq: 2   server text seq: 0   →  Incompatible schema?
```

That would have rejected **every** client on connect and made existing sync rooms fail to load — including clients without this change — and the worker persists that config, so rooms would stay broken after a rollback. The worker now extends the default text schema instead of blanking it, and refuses to blank any default shape type. `syncWorkerRoomSchema.test.ts` pins both directions. The reviewer was also right that my original tests used a hand-rolled schema that would have passed even if the util swap failed; they now derive from `baseShapeUtils`.

242 tests pass, both apps typecheck, `ci:validate` clean.

**I'm blocked on the visual verification.** The skill needs `DG_ROAM_PLAYWRIGHT_{GRAPH_URL,EMAIL,PASSWORD}_1` in `apps/roam/.env`, and that file has none — not in this worktree, not in the main repo, not in any other worktree. There's also no Playwright profile under `local/roam-playwright/profiles/`, so there's no logged-in session for it to reuse. I think "already logged in" refers to your everyday Chrome, which is a separate profile from the one this skill drives. Separately, `~/roam-ext-dev` currently points at the **eng-1884** worktree, so I can't tell which build produced your screenshot.

I won't add credentials myself — passwords are yours to enter — and I won't repoint that symlink without asking, since another session may be using it.

content.text:
Yes — it changes the implementation substantially. Michael's #1442 review targets three things 2227 also does, and Roam has stronger reasons than Obsidian to switch.

## Michael's feedback, applied to 2227

| His point on #1442 | Where 2227 stands now |
|---|---|
| "Changes the built-in text shape's schema, adds a migration, and introduces custom link components" | All three: `TextShapeWithLinkUtil`, migration v6, and a copied `HyperlinkButton`. 2227 also changes the sync worker. |
| "Explore storing the link in `meta.url`… avoid backfilling existing text shapes" | We backfill every text shape in every canvas. |
| "A small pnpm patch if it lets us reuse those components instead of maintaining separate copies" | We keep a copy of `HyperlinkButton` and its icon. |
| "Compare the click behavior to… Discourse nodes" | The link icon opens a new tab. A Roam page link would reload the whole graph in that tab. |
| Loom surfaces: toolbar text, initial link, convert to node | Convert To reads only `props.text` ([uiOverrides.tsx:243](apps/roam/src/components/canvas/uiOverrides.tsx:243)), so the link is silently lost. |
| "Suspicious… how is this related?" | The worker hardening and `syncWorkerRoomSchema.test.ts`, which mirrors worker code without importing it, invite that same question. |

## My 14 Sep reasoning was wrong

I rejected `meta` because downgrading already breaks any canvas migrated to v5, so v6 seemed to cost nothing new. That doesn't hold. Each version bump locks out every collaborator who hasn't updated yet. v5 having done this once doesn't make v6 free.

This matters more in Roam than in Obsidian. A Roam graph has several people editing at once, and Roam Depot updates reach them at different times. When one person's build saves a v6 canvas, a teammate on the previous release gets `Incompatible schema?` and the canvas won't open.

With `meta` neither failure happens. On 14 Sep I tested stock tldraw 2.4.6 against a text shape carrying `meta.url`: it validates, and it round-trips. There's also no version bump. I haven't run an actual older extension build.

## Where Roam differs from Obsidian

- **The sync worker change goes away completely.** This is the biggest gain. The review's release-blocking bug was in that change, and so was the rule that the worker must deploy before the extension. Stock room schemas already accept `meta`, so the worker needs no change at all.
- **Patching is cheaper here.** Roam already patches tldraw 2.4.6, and the patch already re-exports internal components (`ToggleToolLockedButton`, `OverflowingToolbar`, `MobileStylePanel`). So we can export `EditLinkDialog` and `HyperlinkButton` and use them directly. Obsidian had to fork the dialog. Neither component, nor `useHasLinkShapeSelected`, is exported in 2.4.6 today.
- **Page links need no new format.** A Roam page URL is plain `https://`, which `T.linkUrl` already accepts. Obsidian had to work around `obsidian://`. What Roam needs is a click handler: clicking a link to a page in the same graph should navigate inside Roam instead of opening a new tab.
- **Validating the URL becomes our job, and it matters more here.** `props.url` was checked by `T.linkUrl` on every write. `meta` isn't checked at all. In a shared graph, another member or any API writer could store `javascript:` in `meta.url`, and it would reach an `href`. So we check it when saving in the dialog and again before rendering.

## Revised plan

**Remove:** `TextShapeWithLinkUtil`, `baseShapeUtils` and its four call sites, migration v6, all worker changes, the copied icon, `syncWorkerRoomSchema.test.ts` and `textShapeLinkStore.test.ts`. Most of #1441 goes.

**Add:**
1. **Patch additions.** Make `useHasLinkShapeSelected` accept any text shape (`|| type === "text"`). It must not depend on `meta.url` existing: 2228 did that, and a shape could never get its first link. Have `EditLinkDialog` read and write `meta.url` for text shapes. Export `HyperlinkButton`.
2. **Icon overlay.** Rendered from `InFrontOfTheCanvas` next to `DragHandleOverlay`, using the stock `HyperlinkButton`, placed just outside the right edge of the text (the position you liked).
3. **One click listener for geo and text icons.** If the link points to a page in the current graph, intercept the click: plain click opens it in the main window, shift-click opens it in the sidebar. Other URLs open in a new tab as they do now. Every check is based on the result of `new URL`, never a string-prefix test; 2228's bypass came from mixing the two.
4. **Pure helpers in `src/utils/`** for validation, `meta` read/write and page-link parsing. These are easy to unit test, so the `window` stubbing I fought with last time isn't needed.

**Carried over from 2228:** check the rendered screenshot (both tickets shipped the icon on top of the text), hand-edit the patch rather than running `pnpm patch-commit`, and draft any reply to Michael before posting.

**Spin off:** the worker's `{}` blanking is a real trap for future changes, but it doesn't belong in this PR. Creating that ticket needs the Linear connector, which isn't authorised in this session.

questions.question: How should text shapes reuse tldraw's Edit link dialog?

options.label: Patch the stock dialog (Recommended)
options.description: Add about 8 lines to the existing tldraw 2.4.6 patch so EditLinkDialog reads and writes meta.url for text. Nothing is copied, which matches Michael's preference. The catch: if Michael answers 2228's open question the other way, the two apps will differ.

options.label: Fork it like 2228
options.description: Copy the dialog the way 2228 did, so both apps work the same way. That means about 120 lines of copied code to maintain, which Michael said he'd rather avoid.

options.label: Wait for Michael on 2228
options.description: Hold this part until Michael answers 2228's patch-vs-hand-built question, then do the same here.

questions.question: What should clicking a text link to a page in the same graph do?

options.label: Click: main, shift: sidebar (Recommended)
options.description: Same as clicking a Roam page reference. Shift-click matches Discourse nodes (shift opens the sidebar). The icon needs no modifier for a plain click because clicking it doesn't select the shape. Applies to geo links too. External URLs still open a new tab.

options.label: Ctrl: main, shift: sidebar
options.description: Exactly the Discourse node modifiers. A plain click opens a new tab, as it does today.

options.label: Keep new-tab only
options.description: Every link opens a new tab, as it does now. Least work, but it's the inconsistency Michael called poor UX.

questions.question: On 2228 you dropped unit tests. 2227's Done When asks for them. Keep them here?

options.label: Keep, slimmed (Recommended)
options.description: Unit tests for the pure helpers only: URL validation, meta read/write, page-link parsing. This meets 2227's Done When, and these tests need no window stubs.

options.label: Drop, like 2228
options.description: Remove them for consistency with 2228. The fourth Done When item stays unmet; I'd say so in the PR body.

questions.question: When a linked text shape is converted to a Discourse node, what happens to the link?

options.label: Drop it, state it (Recommended)
options.description: Keep the current behaviour and say in the PR that the link is dropped. A Discourse node already opens its own page on click, so a second link would compete with that. Show it in the Loom.

options.label: Carry it over
options.description: Copy meta.url onto the new node. It's kept, but the node gets two click targets, and Discourse nodes don't currently show a link icon.

ENG-2227 Store text shape links in meta and reuse tldraw's link UI

Text shapes keep their link in shape.meta.url, so the stock text schema is
unchanged: no migration, no sync worker change, and a canvas saved by this
build still opens in an older one, which ignores the link and round-trips it.

The existing tldraw patch now makes text shapes eligible for the stock Edit
link action unconditionally (gating on meta.url would stop a shape ever
getting its first link), has EditLinkDialog read and write meta.url for text,
and exports HyperlinkButton. An InFrontOfTheCanvas overlay renders that button
just outside each linked text shape, since text bounds hug their glyphs.

meta has no schema, so the overlay validates with T.linkUrl and renders the
parsed URL; relative paths linkUrl would resolve against a dummy origin are
rejected.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF

can you remind me what are the reasons that we chose to export the shape for the edit link modal instead of patching the TL draw?

Small correction first: for the Edit link modal we patched tldraw rather than exporting it. The thing we exported is `HyperlinkButton`, the link icon. Both changes live in the same `patches/tldraw@2.4.6.patch`.

**Dialog (`EditLinkDialog`): patched in place**

You chose this over forking it the way 2228 did, for four reasons:

- **The dialog's behaviour had to change.** It only knew `props.url`, and text shapes keep their link in `meta.url`. Exporting it would still have left that logic out of reach, so the choice was a patch or a copy.
- **Michael asked for it.** On #1442 he said he'd "consider a small pnpm patch if it lets us reuse those components instead of maintaining separate copies".
- **It's much smaller.** The patch is about 8 lines; a fork is about 120 copied lines that we'd maintain ourselves.
- **Roam already carries a tldraw patch,** so this adds hunks to an existing file rather than a new mechanism.

Cost: Roam now differs from 2228's fork. And the patch breaks on a tldraw upgrade, though Roam is pinned at 2.4.6 and a 2→3 move would be a big project anyway.

**Icon (`HyperlinkButton`): exported, not drawn by a patched text shape**

- **The stock text shape stays untouched.** The icon is drawn from an overlay (Trang's idea on 2228), so there's no `TextShapeUtil` subclass or patched render. That removed `baseShapeUtils` and its "two lists nobody checks agree" risk.
- **Placement is our own logic.** The icon sits just outside the right edge and hides while the shape is selected. Building that into tldraw's render would put app-specific behaviour inside vendor code.
- **No copied component.** Exporting lets the overlay use the real button. The earlier version of 2227 had a hand-copied copy, which is exactly what Michael objected to.
- **There's precedent.** The Roam patch already re-exports internal components (`ToggleToolLockedButton`, `OverflowingToolbar`, `MobileStylePanel`), so one more export follows an existing pattern.

## Reviewer brief

- **Result:** Text shapes get the stock **Edit link** action. Their links open, edit, remove, and persist the same way geo links do, and the icon sits just outside the text's right edge.
- **Review focus:** The link lives in `shape.meta.url` instead of a new prop. The stock text schema is unchanged, so there is no migration and no sync worker change, and a canvas saved by this build still opens in an older one. This follows Michael's review of the Obsidian twin (#1442). The props-schema attempt from earlier on this branch is reverted in `fe3c6266`.
- **Review focus:** `patches/tldraw@2.4.6.patch` adds three changes, and the existing patch hunks are unchanged. Text shapes are always eligible for **Edit link**; gating on `meta.url` would stop a shape from ever getting its first link. `EditLinkDialog` reads and writes `meta.url` for text shapes. `HyperlinkButton` is exported. The dialog is patched rather than copied, which differs from the fork in #1442.
- **Review focus:** `meta` has no schema, so `getTextShapeLinkUrl` is the only check between stored data and the `href`. It renders the parsed URL and rejects `javascript:`, relative, and non-string values.
- **Risk or follow-up:**
  - Links open in a new tab, as geo links do. They do not copy the Discourse node click behaviour; that was a deliberate choice.
  - Converting a linked text shape to a Discourse node drops the link.
  - The icon hides while its shape is selected, so it can't cover the resize and rotate handles.
  - On a fixed-width text box that is wider than its text, the icon sits at the box edge rather than next to the text.
  - Eligibility lives in tldraw itself, so the live run covers it rather than a unit test.

## Verification

Live run in Roam (Playwright, slot 1) on a scratch canvas, which is deleted afterwards. It uses real input events, because tldraw's autosave ignores programmatic store writes.

| Step | Result |
| --- | --- |
| A new text shape from the toolbar shows **Edit link** before it has any link | ✓ |
| Adding a link shows the icon outside the text, vertically centred | ✓ |
| While the shape is selected, the icon hides and the right resize handle works (width 226 → 306) | ✓ |
| Clicking the icon opens the URL in a new tab | ✓ |
| The link is saved in the page's block props | ✓ |
| After closing and reopening the canvas, the icon shows the same URL | ✓ |
| Editing the link updates the `href`, and the props hold only the new URL | ✓ |
| Removing the link hides the icon and clears the URL from props | ✓ |

**Not verified:** a sync-mode canvas; opening in an older extension build (unit-tested against the stock schema only); hiding below 32% zoom; locked, rotated, or frame-clipped text.

# PR evidence upload

Uploads PNGs through `roamAlphaAPI.file.upload` in an authenticated Roam Playwright slot, files them under a page in the slot's graph (`discourse-dev-graph`), and emits a Markdown table that create-pr pastes into the Evidence section.

## When to use

- After verification (Roam `load-extension` run, Obsidian CDP run, manual captures) left PNGs on disk.
- Before create-pr builds the body. Roam PRs: reuse the verification's slot once that run has closed. Obsidian PRs: omit `--slot`.

## Command

Run from the worktree root, using the worktree's own `tsx` so the relative PNG paths and the repo's Playwright resolve:

```sh
./apps/roam/node_modules/.bin/tsx ~/.claude/skills/pr-evidence/upload.ts \
  [--slot N] [--branch <b>] [--label "<YYYY-MM-DD · shortsha · harness>"] [--harness <name>] \
  [--out table.md] [--settle-ms 5000] \
  shot1.png="Empty state" shot2.png="After import" ...
```

- `pnpm --filter roam exec tsx ...` also works, but it changes cwd to `apps/roam`, so pass absolute PNG paths.
- `--branch` defaults to the current git branch. `--label` defaults to `<today> · <short sha> · <--harness or "manual">`.
- Caption defaults to the file name without extension.
- No `--slot`: tries each configured slot (1, 2, 3) and moves on only on a profile-lock error.
- Headless by default (`HEADLESS=false` to watch).

## Output contract

- stdout: JSON `{page, pageUid, branchBlockUid, runBlockUid, items: [{caption, url, blockUid}]}`.
- stderr: `Markdown table: <path>`. The file defaults to `pr-evidence-<runBlockUid>.md` next to the first PNG and contains `| Scenario | Screenshot |` rows with `![caption](url)`. create-pr pastes it as-is.
- URLs are public Firebase storage links (`200 image/png` without cookies, verified 2026-09-23).

## Roam structure

```
Trang test/                       (page, found or created)
  <branch>                        (top-level block, reused on every run)
    <date · sha · harness>        (new run block per invocation, appended last)
      <caption> ![](<url>)        (one per PNG)
```

## Gotchas

- Imports `apps/roam/scripts/playwright/roamSession.ts` from the current worktree (`git rev-parse --show-toplevel`), so profiles live in that worktree's `local/roam-playwright/profiles/` unless `DG_ROAM_PLAYWRIGHT_PROFILE_DIR_<n>` is set.
- A slot's profile can only be open once. Close the verification session first, never delete lock files.
- Login errors (expired session, 2FA) come from `openRoamSession`; recover with `pnpm --filter roam playwright:open -- --slot N --headed --allow-login`, then rerun.
- Never print values from `apps/roam/.env`.
- Uploads cannot be rolled back and Roam cannot list graph files, so don't loop retries on a failing run.
- tsx injects `__name()` into functions passed to `page.evaluate`; the script shims it in the page first. Keep that shim if you edit the in-page code.
